candidates.notes: Experiment 1 is explicitly called a conceptual replication of Baeyens et al. (1990). An overall EC effect was found (significant US valence main effect), but EC effects occurred only for correctly remembered pairings, not for non-remembered pairings. The authors state 'we found no evidence for memory-independent EC overall,' yielding partial support for the original claim and warranting an inconclusive classification.

candidates.original_title: Flavor/flavor and color/flavor conditioning in humans
candidates.description: Pairing tastes with smells produces evaluative conditioning of the smells.
candidates.citation_sentence: In a conceptual replication of the study by Baeyens et al. (1990), we tested whether (1) EC effects occur for smell-taste combinations, (2) whether EC effects are stronger for smell-taste combinations than for visualtaste combinations and (3) whether memory for the pairings and its interaction with CS type is related to the size of the EC effect, and (4) whether there are EC effects of non-remembered CS-US combinations.
candidates.notes: Experiment 1 found an overall EC effect, and the authors said it tentatively supports conditioning olfactory CSs with gustatory USs, although the effect was not isolated from visual CSs. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Flavor/flavor and color/flavor conditioning in humans
candidates.description: Evaluative conditioning from taste pairings is stronger for smells than for visual stimuli.
candidates.citation_sentence: In a conceptual replication of the study by Baeyens et al. (1990), we tested whether (1) EC effects occur for smell-taste combinations, (2) whether EC effects are stronger for smell-taste combinations than for visualtaste combinations and (3) whether memory for the pairings and its interaction with CS type is related to the size of the EC effect, and (4) whether there are EC effects of non-remembered CS-US combinations.
candidates.notes: The smell-versus-visual interaction was nonsignificant. The authors discuss power and possible opposing CS main effects, so this is coded inconclusive rather than failure. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
